LESSON: NUTRITION IN ANIMALS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Living things and their Environment
Topic 2.2: Nutrition in animals

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Nutrition in animals. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do different animals feed?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the structure and functions of different types of teeth
2. classify animals based on their dentition
3. describe the process of digestion in human beings
4. appreciate that animals have varied modes of nutrition

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: NUTRITION IN ANIMALS
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Nutrition in animals helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT ANIMALS
Animals are living things. They move, feed, grow, and respond to their surroundings.
Domestic animals live with people (cow, goat, chicken, dog, cat).
Wild animals live on their own in forests, parks, or water (lion, zebra, fish).
In Kenya you may see cows in a homestead, fish at a market, or birds on the school field.
Safety: do not touch unknown animals; wash hands after handling pets or farm animals.

PART 1: Describe the structure and functions of different types of teeth

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the structure and functions of different types of teeth. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the structure and functions of different types of teeth.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Nutrition in animals” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the structure and functions of different types of teeth. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Classify animals based on their dentition

What this means
In this part you learn to classify animals based on their dentition. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: classify animals based on their dentition.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Nutrition in animals matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can classify animals based on their dentition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe the process of digestion in human beings

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the process of digestion in human beings. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the process of digestion in human beings.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Nutrition in animals this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the process of digestion in human beings. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate that animals have varied modes of nutrition

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate that animals have varied modes of nutrition. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate that animals have varied modes of nutrition.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Nutrition in animals” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate that animals have varied modes of nutrition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Nutrition in animals is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Domestic animals live with people (cow, goat, chicken, dog, cat).

Wild animals live on their own in forests, parks, or water (lion, zebra, fish).

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Nutrition in animals” around your school. (skill: describe the structure and functions of different types of teeth)

Example 2: Say why Nutrition in animals matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: classify animals based on their dentition)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Nutrition in animals this week. (skill: describe the process of digestion in human beings)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Nutrition in animals” around your school. (skill: appreciate that animals have varied modes of nutrition)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Nutrition in animals to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the structure and functions of different types of teeth.
3. Practise this skill: classify animals based on their dentition.
4. Practise this skill: describe the process of digestion in human beings.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Nutrition in animals from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Nutrition in animals: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Nutrition in animals?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do different animals feed?
2. How is food digested in the human body?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Nutrition in animals means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the structure and functions of different types of teeth.
5. Be able to: classify animals based on their dentition.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
